Members of the management body shall, in particular, fulfil the requirements set out in paragraphs 2 to 8.»
actual_answer:
The governance procedures in force regulating the suitability and composition of a credit institution's management body are:

## Primary Governance Procedures

**1. Joint ESMA and EBA Guidelines on the Assessment of the Suitability of Members of the Management Body and Key Function Holders (EBA/GL/2021/06)**

This is the latest version of the guidelines specifically addressing suitability and composition, issued in 2021 by the European Banking Authority (EBA) and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA).

**Key provisions include:**
- Eligibility criteria requiring members of the management body and key function holders to be of good repute and possess adequate knowledge, skills and experience
- Scope covering banks, credit institutions, investment firms (all classes), third-country branches and financial holding companies
- Assessment process requiring institutions to carry out suitability assessments before appointment and on an ongoing basis; competent authorities may also assess suitability
- Compliance and reporting obligations requiring institutions to keep records of assessments and report suitability results to the competent authority
- Time-commitment expectations specifying the annual time commitment expected from each member
- Directorship-counting obligations for compliance with Article 91(3) CRD
- Induction and training requirements: newly appointed members must receive induction within one month and complete training within six months covering ICT-related risks, ESG factors, AI technologies, and diversity
- Mapping of duties requiring institutions to map duties and provide individual statements on responsibilities of each member
- Individual suitability assessment covering reputation, experience, governance criteria (including conflicts of interest and time commitment)
- Collective suitability requirement: the management body as a whole must possess adequate collective knowledge, skills, and experience relevant to the institution's business model, strategy, risk appetite, and activities
- Diversity emphasis: gender-balanced composition is emphasized, and institutions must develop diversity policies
- AML/CTF knowledge: at least one management body member must be responsible for AML implementation, and all members must understand AML/TF risks
- Ongoing monitoring: significant institutions must conduct individual and collective suitability assessments at least annually; less significant institutions at least every two years

**2. EBA Guidelines on Internal Governance (EBA/GL/2021/05)**

This is the latest version issued in 2021, specifying internal governance arrangements, processes, and mechanisms that credit institutions must implement under Article 74(1) of Directive 2013/36/EU (CRD IV/V).

**Key provisions include:**
- Documented roles and duties for each management body member, senior manager, and key function holder
- Requirements for gender diversity and balance in the composition of management bodies
- Individual statements of responsibility for management body members
- A holistic risk management framework subject to independent review
- Oversight of financial reporting integrity and internal control frameworks
- Alignment with CRD VI and the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
- Third-country branches guidance ensuring robust governance frameworks
- Management body responsibilities with enhanced clarity on supervisory and management functions, and conflicts of interest
- Outsourcing arrangements including governance frameworks, due diligence on service providers, and establishment of registers for outsourcing agreements
- Credit institutions must assign at least every three years a review and evaluation of the composition, efficiency, and effectiveness of the management body and its committees to an independent external consultant

## Legal Basis

**Directive 2013/36/EU (CRD IV/V), particularly Article 91**, establishes the legal requirements that members of the management body of a credit institution must meet, including sufficient knowledge, skills, and experience, as well as honesty, integrity, and independence of mind.

**Directive 2014/65/EU (MiFID II)** extends similar corporate governance requirements to investment firms.

## Assessment Procedure

- Credit institutions must assess suitability of management body members prior to appointment and on an ongoing basis, using defined criteria on reputation, experience, and governance
- Competent authorities (e.g., the ECB for significant institutions, national authorities for less significant ones) conduct their own suitability assessments and may refuse authorisation if members do not meet the requirements
- The management body must reflect the knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to fulfil its responsibilities, including understanding of the institution's business, main risks, risk management, financial reporting, and regulatory requirements
- The management body has ultimate and overall responsibility for the credit institution and must define, oversee, and be accountable for governance arrangements ensuring effective and prudent management
- Institutions must have a suitable and transparent organisational and operational structure with effective reporting lines and allocation of responsibilities

## Latest Developments

In February 2026, the EBA and ESMA launched a new consultation on revised joint guidelines on the assessment of suitability of management body members and key function holders, forming part of a broader "Suitability Package" that also includes draft Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS) on documentation requirements for large institutions. The consultation closed on 25 May 2026. The revisions cover proportionality, diversity, reputation, skills, training, and ongoing monitoring requirements.

actual_answer:
## CECA's Stance on Banking Regulation in Spain

**CECA** (Confederación Española de Cajas de Ahorros) is the Spanish association of savings banks and banks created by them, headquartered in Madrid. It represents and defends the interests of its member entities at both national and European levels, engaging with EU institutions in Brussels on issues including banking regulation, financial inclusion, sustainable finance, and social investment.

### Core Regulatory Positions

**1. Regulatory Simplification for Competitiveness**

CECA, together with the other main Spanish banking associations (AEB and UNACC), has been a vocal advocate for **simplifying the European banking regulatory framework** to promote economic growth and EU competitiveness. At a joint event held in Frankfurt, the three associations presented concrete simplification proposals covering financial regulation, digital affairs, and sustainability. CECA's Managing Director Antonio Romero stated: *"Simplification is not an objective in itself; it is the only way to improve European competitiveness and autonomy."*

Key proposals include:
- **Simplification of the macroprudential framework** to avoid duplication between agencies
- **Improvement of accountability** in the regulatory process and incorporation of **ex-post evaluation** of regulations
- **Regulatory proportionality** — ensuring rules are calibrated to the size and complexity of institutions
- **Reduction of the number of capital buffers** and avoidance of overlaps
- A **broader focus for regulators and supervisors**, incorporating a secondary objective of growth and competitiveness alongside financial stability

The associations estimated that regulatory simplification could increase lending by around **€250 billion in Spain alone** and over **€2 trillion across Europe**, potentially lifting euro-zone GDP by 2.7%.

**2. Completion of the Banking Union**

CECA supports completing the EU Banking Union, including the establishment of a **single European Deposit Guarantee Fund (EDIS)** and advancing the **Savings and Investment Union (SIU)**.

**3. Financial Inclusion**

CECA, AEB, and UNACC have actively worked on financial inclusion measures. According to their joint report (based on research by the Valencian Institute of Economic Research — IVIE), **99.3% of the Spanish population has access to banking services**. CECA advocates for proximity banking and measures to bridge the digital divide, particularly for elderly populations.

**4. Sustainable Finance**

CECA participates in sustainable finance initiatives and supports the EU's sustainability goals, while calling for the sustainable finance framework to remain **proportionate and competitive**. CECA's member foundations constitute the leading private social investor in Spain through their "Obra Social" programmes.

**5. Digital Regulation and Payments**

CECA co-organises events on the **Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)** and RegTech trends, and supports the interconnection of European payment systems. Together with AEB and UNACC, CECA backs the Bizum platform's integration with 13 European countries and advocates for European sovereignty in payment systems.

**6. Academic Research on Regulation's Impact**

CECA has launched a joint academic chair with the **Pontifical University of Comillas** to promote research on the economic impact of banking regulation, aiming to provide rigorous evidence to the public debate on how regulation affects lending, competitiveness, and the real economy.

### EU-Level Engagement

CECA maintains active representation in Brussels and is affiliated with the **European Savings and Retail Banking Group (ESBG)** and the **World Savings and Retail Banking Institute (WSBI)**. It contributes position papers, participates in EU consultations, and engages with the European Banking Authority (EBA) on prudential regulation topics. During the 2023 Spanish Presidency of the EU Council, CECA published a priorities document covering solvency, sustainability, financial markets, AML/CFT, payments, digital banking, and Banking Union.

## Revolut App Reviews: What Users Value and Complain About

Based on analysis of Revolut app reviews, here's what users value and complain about:

### Overall Ratings
As of September 2026, Revolut holds a **4.8–4.9 out of 5** rating across app stores, with over **200,000–329,000 reviews** depending on the region. Overall user sentiment is positive, though recurring pain points persist.

---

### What Users Value Most

1. **Speed and ease of use** — Users consistently praise the app for being intuitive, simple, and feature-rich. Long-term users describe it as their primary banking app, even over traditional bank accounts.

2. **International capabilities** — Multi-currency support, interbank exchange rates, and seamless use abroad are among the most-cited benefits. Travelling and sending money internationally are top use cases.

3. **All-in-one financial management** — Users appreciate managing daily finances, transfers, crypto, and investments in a single app.

4. **Security features** — Single-use virtual cards for online shopping, two-factor authentication, and 24/7 fraud monitoring are highlighted as valued protections.

5. **Continuous improvement** — Multiple reviewers note that Revolut keeps adding features and improving quality over time.

**User quotes:**
- *"It's simple, full of features, and easy to use."* — Michael, UK
- *"The app makes my financial life much simpler and more secure."* — Carolina, Italy
- *"Revolut is amazing. It's my main account for travelling or sending money abroad. Service is fast, customer support is helpful, and Revolut keeps improving in quality."* — Pawel, Japan
- *"I've been using Revolut for the past 5 years and it's my main account, even though I have 4+ accounts."* — Michael, UK

---

### Common Complaints and Pain Points

1. **Customer support quality** — This is the most persistent complaint. Users report slow responses, over-reliance on AI chatbots and scripted answers, and difficulty reaching a human agent — especially when locked out of their account.

2. **Account restrictions and frozen funds** — Users report accounts being frozen or restricted without clear explanation, with funds inaccessible while compliance checks run. Resolution can be slow.

3. **Hidden fees** — Complaints about unexpected charges, particularly around crypto transactions and subscription cancellations.

4. **Fraud and scam complaints** — Revolut has led UK fraud complaint tables for three consecutive years. In 2025, customers brought **3,208 fraud complaints** to the Financial Ombudsman Service (1,875 authorised push payment fraud and 1,333 unauthorised fraud). The FOS uphold rate for Revolut APP fraud cases was **37%**.

5. **Data privacy concerns** — Users have raised concerns about Revolut sharing data with third-party apps. Most recently (September 2026), a security incident involved attackers using a fake government email to obtain sensitive customer data — including ID documents, verification selfies, account details, and transaction histories.

6. **Difficulty deleting accounts** — Some users report challenges when trying to close their accounts or access support after being locked out.

---

### Summary

Revolut is widely valued for its speed, international money features, and all-in-one convenience, earning very high app store ratings. However, customer support responsiveness, account freezing practices, fraud handling, and recent data security incidents remain significant areas of user concern.

## ECB Official Interest Rates

As of **16 September 2026**, the ECB's official interest rates are:

| Facility | Rate |
|---|------|
| **Deposit facility** | **2.50%** |
| **Main refinancing operations** | **2.65%** |
| **Marginal lending facility** | **2.90%** |

These rates were set following the ECB Governing Council's decision on **10 September 2026** to raise the three key interest rates by **25 basis points**. This was the **second rate hike in 2026** (the first occurred in June, when the deposit rate was raised to 2.25%), reversing an easing cycle that had brought rates down eight times between June 2024 and mid-2025.

The rate increases were driven by rising inflation pressures linked to the conflict in the Middle East, which pushed eurozone headline inflation to **3.3% in August 2026** (with energy inflation at 14.3%). ECB staff projections from September 2026 forecast headline inflation averaging **3.0% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027, and 2.1% in 2028**, with GDP growth of **0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027, and 1.5% in 2028**.

The ECB noted that a 2.5% deposit rate sits at the **upper bound of its neutral rate estimate**, meaning any further tightening would move policy into restrictive territory. Markets are pricing in approximately a 75% probability of another rate increase in October or December 2026.

---

## Latest M3 Monetary Aggregate

The most recent ECB release on **27 August 2026** shows the **three-month annualised M3 growth rate rose to 3.2% in July 2026**, up from a revised 3.0% in June 2026.

### Recent M3 Trend (2025–2026)

| Period | M3 Annual Growth (YoY) |
|---|------|
| November 2025 | 3.0% (stock: ~€17.2 trillion) |
| February 2026 | ~3.0% (stock: ~€17.3 trillion) |
| March 2026 | 3.2% |
| April 2026 | 3.0% |
| May 2026 | 3.2% |
| June 2026 | 3.0% |
| **July 2026** | **3.2%** |

M3 growth has been oscillating in a narrow **3.0%–3.2% band** throughout 2026, reflecting steady but moderate monetary expansion across the 20-nation euro area.

### Key M3 Components

- **M1 (narrow money):** Growth pulled back slightly in recent months (e.g., 4.6% in March 2026, down from 4.8% in February), indicating some moderation in the most liquid deposits.

- **M2–M1 (short-term deposits other than overnight):** Declines have been narrowing, with the contraction easing from −1.8% in October 2025 to −0.8% by November 2025.

- **M3–M2 (marketable instruments):** Growth has been volatile but generally positive, reaching 4.5% in March 2026.

- **Private-sector credit:** Claims on the private sector contributed approximately 3.0 percentage points to total M3 growth in March 2026, making it the primary driver of money supply expansion. Corporate lending growth reached a 3-year high by mid-2026.

### What M3 Measures

M3 is the broadest monetary aggregate tracked by the ECB. It encompasses currency in circulation, overnight deposits (M1), short-term time and savings deposits (M2), plus large time deposits, institutional money market funds, repurchase agreements, and short-term debt securities. The ECB monitors M3 as part of its "two-pillar" monetary analysis framework, viewing large swings in M3 as signals of shifts in financial system liquidity and credit conditions.

M3 growth at the current ~3% level is generally considered consistent with an inflation rate near the ECB's 2% target over the medium term, though transmission lags mean the full impact may take time to materialise. Despite the ECB's rate hikes in 2026, lending has continued to grow, suggesting underlying demand remains robust enough to absorb higher borrowing costs.

## Brazil CNPJ: Tax Compliance Status, Company Address & Activity Verification

### What Is a CNPJ?

The **CNPJ** (*Cadastro Nacional da Pessoa Jurídica*) is Brazil's 14-digit federal company tax identification number, administered by the **Receita Federal do Brasil** (Brazilian Federal Revenue Service). Every legally operating company in Brazil must hold an active CNPJ. As of July 2026, Brazil had roughly **25.2 million active CNPJs** according to the government's Mapa de Empresas dashboard.

A CNPJ is required to:

- File federal, state, and municipal taxes
- Issue electronic invoices (Nota Fiscal Eletrônica / NF-e)
- Register for state VAT (ICMS) and municipal service tax (ISS)
- Open business bank accounts
- Sign contracts and participate in public procurement
- Conduct import/export operations

---

### How to Verify a CNPJ — Official Process

The official, free verification is done through the Receita Federal's **"Emissão de Comprovante de Inscrição e de Situação Cadastral"** portal:

1. Go to the Receita Federal CNPJ consultation page
2. Enter the **14-digit CNPJ** number
3. Complete the **CAPTCHA** verification
4. Click **"Consultar"**
5. Review the certificate the system displays

The returned certificate includes:

| Data Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Registration status** | Active (*Ativa*), Suspended (*Suspensa*), Unfit (*Inapta*), or Closed (*Baixada*) |
| **Legal name** (*Razão Social*) | Official registered company name |
| **Trade name** (*Nome Fantasia*) | Commercial/brand name |
| **Registered address** | Full address including city, state, and postal code |
| **Primary CNAE code** | Main business activity classification |
| **Secondary CNAE codes** | Additional registered business activities |
| **Partners/Administrators (QSA)** | Names of partners and administrators |
| **Opening date** | Date the company was registered |
| **Legal nature** | Type of legal entity |
| **Share capital** | Registered capital amount |

This consultation is governed by **Instrução Normativa RFB nº 2.119/2022** and is completely free.

---

### CNPJ Registration Statuses Explained

- **Ativa (Active):** The company is in good standing and legally permitted to operate
- **Suspensa (Suspended):** Operations are temporarily frozen, typically due to compliance issues
- **Inapta (Unfit):** The company has missed multiple mandatory filings (e.g., DCTF or ECF). This status freezes the ability to issue invoices, can lead to bank account restrictions, and effectively halts business operations
- **Baixada (Closed):** The CNPJ has been formally deactivated/dissolved

---

### Consequences of Non-Compliance

If a company misses multiple DCTF or ECF filings, the Receita Federal can mark the CNPJ as **"inapta"**. Consequences include:

- Loss of ability to issue invoices
- Bank accounts may be frozen
- Business operations effectively stop

To regularize, the company must identify all missing returns, calculate back taxes and penalties, file everything retroactively, and pay debts or arrange installment plans. Only after the Receita Federal accepts the filings and debts does the CNPJ status return to "Ativa."

---

### Additional Verification Resources

- **SINTEGRA / SEFAZ portals:** For verifying state-level tax registrations (*Inscrição Estadual*), needed for ICMS/VAT compliance in each Brazilian state
- **Simples Nacional portal:** To check whether a company is enrolled in the simplified tax regime for micro and small enterprises (includes Simples Nacional and MEI flags)
- **CNPJ compliance checks** can also verify against federal sanction lists such as **CEIS** (sanctioned companies), **CNEP** (penalized companies), and **CEPIM** (irregular non-profits), as well as Leniency Agreements

---

### Key Takeaway

Verifying a Brazilian company's CNPJ through the Receita Federal portal is the authoritative way to confirm its **tax compliance status**, **registered address**, and **business activities (CNAE codes)** before entering into any business relationship. An **"Ativa"** status confirms the entity is legally registered and in good standing with federal tax authorities.

## Market Earnings by Occupation: Managers & Senior Roles — Benchmarking Overview

### Key Compensation Benchmarks

Based on the latest available data (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, May 2024–May 2025 estimates), here are representative earnings benchmarks for managerial and senior roles:

| Occupation | Median Annual Salary | Notes |

| **Construction Managers** | ~$106,980 (median) | BLS May 2024 data |
| **Finance Managers (Australia)** | ~A$2,904/week median (full-time) | Per Jobs and Skills Australia, May 2025 survey |

### Broader Context

- **Salary budget increases** across industries are projected at approximately **3.5% for 2025–2026**, though actual adjustments vary by market conditions and geography.
- **Management occupations** consistently rank among the highest-paid major occupation groups. BLS reported an annual mean wage of **$65,360 for construction and extraction occupations** overall (May 2025), while management and engineering roles within those industries sit significantly above that level.
- **Geographic variation** is substantial — high-cost metro areas (New York, San Francisco, Washington D.C.) can push managerial compensation 30%+ above national medians.

### Benchmarking Considerations

When benchmarking senior management compensation:

- **Use occupation-specific data** rather than broad industry averages, as pay varies widely even within the same sector.
- **Account for total compensation**, including bonuses, equity, and benefits, which can represent a significant portion of senior-level pay.
- **Match data sources carefully** — different surveys may report mean vs. median wages, cover different time periods, or include different populations (self-reported vs. employer-reported).
- **Update regularly** — annual survey data from 2023–2024 may not accurately reflect 2025–2026 market conditions due to shifts in labor demand, interest rates, and regional economic trends.

Os fundos acumulados na Suíça integravam também pagamentos determinados pelo arguido RICARDO SALGADO, com a mobilização de quantias oriundas de entidades em offshore que pertenciam ao Grupo Espírito Santo. Tais pagamentos estavam relacionados com intervenções de JOSÉ SÓCRATES, enquanto primeiro-ministro, em favor da estratégia definida por RICARDO SALGADO para o grupo Portugal Telecom, do qual o BES era acionista.

Tal utilização passava, designadamente, por levantamentos e entregas de quantias em numerário a JOSÉ SÓCRATES, as quais eram efetuadas com a intervenção de CARLOS SANTOS SILVA mas também dos arguidos INÊS DO ROSÁRIO, JOÃO PERNA e GONÇALO FERREIRA.

Esses fundos foram, igualmente, utilizados para aquisição de imóveis, obras de arte, pagamento de viagens, aquisições de exemplares do livro de JOSÉ SÓCRATES e para fazer chegar dinheiro a pessoas das relações deste arguido.

Para além dos pagamentos acima referidos em benefício de JOSÉ SÓCRATES, RICARDO SALGADO determinou também que fossem efetuados pagamentos aos arguidos ZEINAL BAVA e HENRIQUE GRANADEIRO. Nesse período, entre 2006 e 2010, estes arguidos exerceram funções na administração da Portugal Telecom, tendo aceitado esses pagamentos para agir em conformidade com interesses definidos por RICARDO SALGADO para o BES enquanto acionista da PT.

Ainda com origem no Grupo Espírito Santo, e por determinação de RICARDO SALGADO, já em 2010 e 2011, CARLOS SANTOS SILVA terá montado um esquema, em conjunto com JOAQUIM BARROCA e HÉLDER BATAGLIA, com vista à atribuição de nova quantia a favor de JOSÉ SÓCRATES. Esse esquema passava pela produção de um contrato promessa de compra e venda de um edifício em Angola. Através do incumprimento dessa contrato promessa e consequentemente perda do sinal, foi justificada a transferência de uma quantia para as contas do grupo LENA que ficou com o encargo de devolver o mesmo montante a CARLOS SANTOS SILVA ou a sociedades do mesmo, para este, por sua vez, fazer chegar o dinheiro a JOSÉ SÓCRATES.

O Ministério Público, do Departamento Central de Investigação e Ação Penal, proferiu nove despachos de arquivamento, nomeadamente em relação ao arguidos João Abrantes Serra, Joaquim Paulo da Conceição e Paulo Lalanda e Castro. No total, o Ministério Público decidiu extrair 15 certidões, para posterior investigação em processo autónomo.

O despacho final tem mais de 4 mil páginas.

Ao longo do inquérito foram efetuadas cerca de duas centenas de buscas, inquiridas mais de 200 testemunhas e recolhidos dados bancários sobre cerca de 500 contas, quer domiciliadas em Portugal quer no Estrangeiro. Foi igualmente recolhida vasta documentação quer em suporte de papel, quer digital.

- Issue invoices (notas fiscais)
- Open business bank accounts

- **CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas)**: Individual taxpayer number (format: XXX.XXX.XXX-XX)
- **RG Number**: Individual identity document
- **Case Numbers**: For litigation and legal proceedings
- **State Registration Numbers**: For state-level tax compliance
